purpose: Editorial explanations of recorded development methods, not new evidence or model outputs. Scores are read only from research-20261105.json.

stories.task_name: What happens if an object is removed?

evidence.text: With gray removed, the pink hole-sensor event occurs at 1.43-1.44 s.
Sensor entry does not establish that pink eventually stays in the hole.

stories.takeaway: Explicit event meaning improves the local comparison.
stories.limit: The 72.14% score includes two perfect categorical checks; the 40 slider questions alone score 44.28%.
stories.comparison_note: All answers use the 27B reasoner. The matched factual-event baselines are retained under Detailed metrics & ablations.
stories.reference_note: Source positions, velocities, gravity and scene geometry feed the same event-semantic method. Five-second events, including object-removal events, are model-derived, not observed outcome GT. Source headers differ between arms; this is not a verified upper bound. Slider-only R²: predicted 44.28%, reference 33.91%.

evidence.text: In the illustrated saved case, computation stops at 6.43271 s at an unsupported contact.
No complete exit is established; this does not prove B would never exit.

stories.takeaway: Contact-by-contact timelines outperform all recorded local code controls.
stories.limit: Only eight questions. The intervention starts from assumed observed motion; explanation faithfulness is still incomplete.
stories.comparison_note: All conditions share the same source-derived mechanism rules.
stories.reference_note: Reference geometry passes through the conditional-timeline method. Geometry is partial; body approximations and unsupported contacts remain.

stories.task_name: Would B pass the gate after removing A?

evidence.text: A is removed. The computed path reaches a fitting gate crossing at 6.0664 s.
Observed B motion initializes the model; factual block motion is retained.

stories.takeaway: The timeline improves over video and full code; the direct-code comparison is unresolved.
stories.limit: Direct-code answers are constant, making its R² undefined. The crossing is modeled, not observed ground truth.
stories.comparison_note: Shared source rules. Undefined correlation is missing, not a zero-length score.
stories.reference_note: Factual-reference state uses the same numerical execution and answer schema. It is not GT for the unobserved counterfactual world.

stories.task_name: Could a different path reach the goal?

evidence.text: For the saved blue-path case, the goal is reachable at action 7 even with unknown future door states closed; recorded states stay unchanged.
Door timing is assumed unaffected by the player's choice. A feasible route is not a predicted choice.

stories.takeaway: Route calculations add value beyond the same observed-state graph.
stories.limit: Older video/code controls have less observation coverage; full-code R² is undefined. This is not a clean all-control win.
stories.comparison_note: Video/direct/full-code controls have less observation coverage. The graph-only ablation uses the same facts and remains in the detailed metrics.
stories.reference_note: 93.89% uses an earlier reference-JSON presentation. Current same-method reference inputs duplicate predicted inputs, so no independent matched GT result is established.

stories.task_name: Will contact occur after the scene disappears?

evidence.text: Describe ball, goal, slide and container, with time-bound relative positions.
The graph ends at disappearance. Future contact remains for the VLM to judge.

stories.takeaway: Complete-scene evidence improves over the clarified video control, but ties historical direct code.
stories.limit: Equally clarified direct-code and full-code controls were not run. The graph does not simulate the future.
stories.comparison_note: Historical direct code uses different wording; unmeasured controls cannot establish superiority.
stories.reference_note: Reference input uses the complete-scene graph and prospective clarification. Dynamic GT covers the initial state only, not the full motion.

stories.task_name: How did A contribute to B's exit?

evidence.text: Before event E1 at 2.44 s: A=(394.50, 219.50), B=(438.50, 305.50), in image pixels.
These are actual observations, not a scene with A removed or proof of causation.

stories.takeaway: Event-local positions improve the result, but not enough to pass the preset gate.
stories.limit: The gain over dense notes is 9.48 pp, below the frozen 10 pp requirement. Added pixel measurements also change perception coverage.
stories.comparison_note: Our method adds pixel measurements, so this is not a representation-only comparison. Dense event notes and other ablations remain in the detailed metrics.
stories.reference_note: Replace factual ball geometry with reference data and keep the same event-path renderer. Other scene fields are not replaced by complete GT.

stories.task_name: How surprising is the physical event?

evidence.text: At 2.88 s, the pair-center observation becomes unavailable.
The target's before/after velocities are unknown; missing detection is not physical disappearance.

stories.takeaway: The predicted graph does not improve surprise judgments.
stories.limit: Signed r is negative. Clean direct/full-code controls are unavailable; five examples do not establish general behavior.
stories.comparison_note: R² hides correlation direction. Here the graph's signed r is -0.1690.
stories.reference_note: Recovered visible-reference observations use the same image-graph method. Hidden motion, physical identity and latent properties are not fully certified.

stories.task_name: Who faces the harder shot toward the gate?

evidence.text: The hypothetical blue-to-marble center segment intersects the supplied barrier box.
Finite-body access and reaching the gate are not established by this test.

stories.takeaway: Geometry calculations help the graph baseline, but remain below direct code.
stories.limit: Eight question variants use only two diagrams. Segment intersection alone is not physical difficulty.
stories.comparison_note: The paired graph improvement does not establish superiority over direct code.
stories.reference_note: Source-corrected reference geometry uses the same segment-intersection operator. Two diagrams underlie eight variants; this is not complete physical-action GT.
